headline: ALL SIX LME CONTRACTS SURGE: Copper Rebounds to $6.40 as Trump Flags Iran Weekend Deal
snippet: Copper futures climbed back to approximately $6.40/lb on June 12, recovering from three-week lows as President Trump told reporters a US-Iran peace agreement — including Strait of Hormuz reopening — could be signed as early as this weekend. All six main London Metal Exchange contracts posted gains alongside a rally in Asian equities, with the copper rebound carrying particularly high stakes for the junior mining sector: a confirmed Hormuz deal would remove the energy-inflation shock driving the 70% December rate-hike probability that has suppressed commodity equities since May. For investors in copper-adjacent juniors, the intraday move from $6.20 to $6.40 represents the market pricing the first leg of a two-catalyst recovery — deal confirmation followed by Warsh's FOMC tone next Wednesday — before the structural 491,000-tonne annual deficit narrative fully reasserts itself.

headline: SILVER ACT: 40+ Industry Coalition Urges Congress to End Single-Region Precious Metals Storage Risk
snippet: A 40-plus company coalition spanning depositories, mints, dealers, refiners, miners, logistics providers, banks, and insurers submitted a letter to congressional leaders on June 11, 2026 calling on Congress to advance the bipartisan SILVER Act (System Integrity through Licensed Vault Expansion and Resilience Act), which would mandate two approved precious metals depositories in each of the Mountain, Pacific, Eastern, and Central time zones — ending the current situation where no CFTC-approved depository exists outside a narrow sub-region of the northeastern U.S. Senators Cortez Masto (D-NV) and Risch (R-ID) and CFTC Chairman Michael Selig have endorsed the bill; the coalition argues the geographic concentration poses a systemic market and national security risk because significant gold and silver mining, minting, processing, and trading already takes place in the Western U.S., where producers and dealers cannot access regulated futures settlement infrastructure at comparable cost to eastern counterparts. For junior mining investors, passage would directly reduce basis risk and physical delivery costs for silver and gold producers with operations in Nevada, Idaho, Colorado, and other western mining states.

headline: 5.0 g/t Au OVER 10.85m: Galway Metals Expands North Deposit With 34 Holes at Clarence Stream NB
snippet: Galway Metals Inc. (TSXV: GWM) reported June 10 assay results from 34 diamond drill holes at the North Deposit of its Clarence Stream high-grade gold project in New Brunswick — headline intercepts include 5.0 g/t Au over 10.85 metres and an ultra-high-grade sub-interval of 40.3 g/t Au over 1.55 metres, with gold mineralisation confirmed continuously in the northern extension area beyond the limits of the existing 2022 resource. The project currently hosts a combined 2.234 million ounce resource (922,000 oz Indicated at 2.3 g/t and 1.334 Moz Inferred at 2.6 g/t) across approximately 65 kilometres of highly prospective strike, and the North Deposit extension results open a material resource-growth path heading into planned 2026 follow-up drilling. Clarence Stream has also intersected antimony mineralisation in the western pit-constrained zone — making it one of the few Canadian projects with simultaneous gold-antimony discovery potential at a time when antimony is on every critical minerals list.

headline: PERFECT SCORE IN PERU: All 5 Camino Holes Hit Copper — 76.2m at 0.88% Cu, 16.25m at 2.67% Cu at Adriana
snippet: Camino Minerals Corporation (TSXV: COR) announced June 10 Phase 2 drilling results from the Adriana target at the Costa de Cobre IOCG copper project on Peru's southern coast — all five holes intercepted copper mineralisation across approximately 400 metres of strike to maximum depths of 260 metres, with best hole DCH-133 returning 76.2 metres grading 0.88% Cu including 16.25 metres at 2.67% Cu and 6.82 g/t Ag. The 100% hit rate over 400 metres of strike extent confirms broad, laterally continuous IOCG-style copper mineralisation at Adriana and expands the known footprint of Costa de Cobre's highest-grade corridor. In a copper market where Jefferies forecasts a sustained 491,000-tonne annual deficit through 2030 and COMEX Section 232 tariff premiums benefit North American and allied-jurisdiction producers, a 100% hole success rate in a IOCG system at this scale — historically the template for deposits in the 100–500 million pound range — positions Adriana as a Phase 3 priority target.

headline: DISCOVERY CONFIRMED: Rocky Shore's Lane Pond Gold Zone Hit in 8 of 13 Holes — Drill Program Triples to 12,500m
snippet: Rocky Shore Gold Ltd. (CSE: RSG) announced June 10 that reconnaissance drilling at the Lane Pond Gold Target within its Gold Anchor Project in Newfoundland has confirmed a near-surface bulk-style gold zone in eight of 13 widely spaced drill holes, with the mineralised system now defined over 400 metres of strike, 600 metres down-dip, and 50 to 240 metres of vertical extent — open in all directions. In response to the multi-hole confirmation, the company has tripled its planned drill program from 3,500 metres to 12,500 metres, targeting both the bulk envelope and higher-grade structurally controlled zones interpreted to feed the broad system. The Lane Pond Target sits within an 11-kilometre north-trending VTEM geophysical anomaly that was largely untested before this program — a scale of untested strike that suggests the current discovery defines only the shallowest expression of a potentially much larger gold system associated with the Appleton Fault corridor.

headline: 350m STRIKE EXTENDED: Brunswick Drills 27.4m at 1.13% Li2O — Anais Dyke Final Winter Results at Anatacau
snippet: Brunswick Exploration Inc. (TSXV: BRW) released June 10 final assay results from its 2026 winter drill campaign at the Anatacau Main Project in Quebec — hole AN-26-12 intersected six stacked, well-mineralised pegmatite dykes including a continuous 27.4-metre interval grading 1.13% Li2O at a shallow vertical depth of only 90 metres, extending the Anais Main dyke to over 350 metres of continuously drilled strike length while the system remains open in all directions. The winter campaign consisted of seven holes totalling over 1,800 metres; future drilling is planned for late Q3 2026 following a campaign at the nearby Mirage target. At the current gold-silver ratio of approximately 64:1, the market's focus is largely on precious metals — but lithium carbonate above $24,000/tonne has returned commercial viability to Quebec hardrock pegmatite projects, and a continuous shallow system grading above 1% Li2O over 350+ metres of strike represents the kind of resource-scalable geometry that acquirers in the emerging North American battery supply chain are actively seeking.

headline: NEVADA WALKER LANE: Walker River Starts 10,000m RC at Lapon Canyon Gold — First 43-101 Resource by Year-End
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Walker River Resources
snippet: Walker River Resources Corp. (TSXV: WRR) announced June 11 the commencement of its 2026 reverse circulation drill program at the Lapon Canyon Gold Project, located within Nevada's Walker Lane Gold Trend approximately 60 km southeast of Yerington — an initial 10,000-metre campaign designed to complete both resource-expansion infill and exploration step-out holes testing deeper intrusive-related targets including prospective monzonitic and porphyritic phases identified in 2025. A property-wide airborne magnetic and radiometric survey has also been completed, with interpretation ongoing to refine targeting and evaluate the potential for additional mineralised systems at depth. The program's explicit goal is delivering a first NI 43-101 compliant mineral resource estimate before year-end 2026 — a completion milestone that would re-rate the project from exploration to resource-stage in the Nevada Tier 1 jurisdiction that currently commands the highest acquisition premiums among North American gold districts.

headline: JAMES BAY LITHIUM EXPANSION: Critical Elements Drills 10,000m at Rose West — 3 New Spodumene Bodies Targeted
snippet: Critical Elements Lithium Corp. (TSXV: CRE) announced June 9 the launch of Phase 2 of its 10,000-metre summer drill program at the Rose West Discovery, located approximately 10 km west of its flagship Rose Lithium-Tantalum Project in Eeyou Istchee, Quebec — targeting three newly identified spodumene-bearing pegmatitic bodies to expand the mineralised footprint and define the geometry of the Phase 1 discovery. Rose itself has a completed August 2023 Feasibility Study, key permits, formalized agreements with Cree First Nations neighbours, and existing infrastructure, making it one of North America's most advanced undeveloped hardrock lithium projects; Rose West represents the incremental resource-growth pathway that could improve the project economics required for a final investment decision in the current lithium price environment. Systematic drilling of three new pegmatite bodies 10 km from an already-permitted project represents the lowest-risk near-term lithium resource growth available in the Quebec critical minerals corridor.

headline: VOISEY'S BAY CONNECTION: Viridian Metals Launches 50-Hole Cu-Ni-Co Drill at Kraken, Labrador
snippet: Viridian Metals Corp. announced June 9 that diamond drilling has commenced at its Kraken Copper-Nickel-Cobalt Project in Labrador — a 50-hole program designed to systematically infill between widely spaced holes along the five-kilometre Main Zone conductive corridor, where prior drilling has intersected copper grades up to 4.15% Cu within a magmatic sulfide system hosted by the same intrusive suite that contains Vale's Voisey's Bay deposit, approximately 75 km to the north. The 2026 program targets both the conversion of broadly spaced intercepts into a continuous drill-defined mineralised footprint and extensions of the known copper-nickel-cobalt zones at depth and along strike. The geological parallel to Voisey's Bay is significant: Voisey's Bay is one of the highest-grade nickel-copper-cobalt deposits in the Western Hemisphere, and the presence of magmatic sulfide mineralisation in the same intrusive package at Kraken indicates the same fundamental mineralising process was active across a 75-km corridor — with Kraken's 35-km strike length suggesting meaningful inventory potential if the system is mineralised throughout.

headline: TWO RIGS IN YUKON: Blue Jay Gold Targets Skukum Creek Ag-Au Corridor and Historic High-Grade Raca Zone
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Blue Jay Gold
snippet: Blue Jay Gold Corp. (TSXV: JAY) announced June 11 the commencement of diamond drilling at the Steller Gold Project in the Yukon Territory, with an initial rig already turning on the northern silver-gold-rich zone around the Raca target on the Skukum Creek Corridor and a second rig mobilising to site. The Skukum Creek Corridor is a well-established Yukon precious metals belt with historic high-grade intercepts, and Blue Jay's 2026 program is targeting the Raca zone as the primary silver-gold target before expanding to broader exploration objectives across the property. With silver at $67/oz following a six-consecutive-year supply deficit and no major new Yukon silver-dominant discoveries in the public domain, a new high-grade Ag-Au discovery on the Skukum Creek Corridor would represent one of the highest-impact exploration outcomes available in the current market cycle.
